body: Hub code lives in crates/cctg as a lib+bin package (src/lib.rs exposes pub mod hub; main.rs calls cctg::hub::run). Alternative: modules only under the bin with #[allow(dead_code)] for the API surface TASK-009/011 will use, or a separate hub crate. Lib target keeps clippy -D warnings clean without allow attributes and lets the scratch RSS probe link the real code.

Message bucket = capacity 5, refill 1 token per 4 s, min gap 1 s. Any 60 s window then has at most 5 + 15 = 20 sends. Alternative: capacity 20 with 1 token per 3 s allows up to ~39 sends in a window (mutation capacity 20 fails the window test); capacity 1 at 3 s is correct but makes a 3-chunk reply take 6 s.

Any 429 pauses the whole outbound queue for retry_after and puts the job back at the head of its lane; retry is unlimited but one attempt per retry_after. Alternative: per-lane pause or capped retries. One chat, one bot: flood wait is not lane-specific, and a per-lane pause would let other lanes keep hitting the same flood window.

getUpdates result is decoded as Vec<serde_json::Value> and each update is parsed separately; a bad update becomes Ignored::Malformed and still advances the offset. Alternative: typed Vec<Update>, where one wrong-typed field fails the whole batch and polling refetches it forever.

Idle RSS measured with scratch/planner/rss_probe (real getMe/getChatMember/getForumTopicIconStickers over TLS + running scheduler, no getUpdates) instead of running the real hub: getWebhookInfo shows 2 pending updates, and the hub poll loop would confirm them. Alternative: run cctg hub for 60 s against the real bot.

tests/stdout.rs: hub is removed from the success loop and gets its own test (no config -> non-zero exit, stdout empty, stderr names CCTG_BOT_TOKEN), run in an empty CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR dir with CCTG_* removed. Alternative: keep hub a no-op when config is missing, which hides a misconfigured hub.

reqwest 0.13 with default-features=false and features json, multipart, rustls (aws-lc-rs provider). Alternative: reqwest 0.12 rustls-tls (ring) or rustls-no-provider + explicit ring. 0.13 builds offline from the local registry cache on this host in 45.6 s clean release; no extra crate needed.

Same-topic FIFO fix: keep one Message VecDeque (global FIFO for sends and documents) and pick a permission prompt only when no older job of its thread_id is queued (linear scan, remove(index), push_front on 429). Chosen over PLAN_V2 per-topic queues with sequence numbers: same semantics, one queue less, fewer moving parts.

Flaky routing_logs_never_contain_user_ids (56/100 failures in the reference) moved to its own integration test binary tests/routing_logs.rs. Alternative tracing::callsite::rebuild_interest_cache() inside the unit test rejected: it only narrows the cross-thread callsite-registration race, it does not remove it.

Dropped PLAN_V2 bounded mailbox drain: no reproducible starvation, producers are bounded by a 1024 channel and Telegram/agent traffic; changing it is unverifiable churn. Kept try_recv drain as in the reference.

Considered sanitizing ApiError::Decode (serde_json invalid-type text can echo a value). Rejected: strictly decoded responses only carry the bot own id/chat id/our own text; updates with user ids go through route_batch which discards the error. No path reaches a user id or the token secret.
Initial flake-check script was rejected by PowerShell because an interpolated variable was immediately followed by a colon; fixed by delimiting the variable name.

Second flake-check attempt was rejected because Windows PowerShell promoted cargo stderr diagnostics to NativeCommandError under Stop; changed executable discovery to parse stdout JSON and discard ordinary stderr diagnostics while checking the exit code.

Redirecting cargo stderr alone still produced NativeCommandError under the script-wide Stop preference; executable discovery now temporarily relaxes ErrorActionPreference around cargo and restores it before validating the exit code.
Flake runner selected the last Cargo executable artifact, which was the cctg binary harness and rejected -q; changed discovery to require the expected Cargo target name and kind for each harness.

Bounded scheduler fairness uses a four-job unmetered streak and is checked only after an eligible permission prompt. Alternative: unconditional lane alternation, rejected because it can send an ordinary message before ready permission traffic and violate permission-first.

QA verified scheduler fairness with a step-driver harness (copy of Scheduler::run inside the test module of a scratch workspace copy) that checks priority/FIFO/bucket invariants at every dispatch, over 120 random mixed-traffic scenarios with 429s. Alternative: black-box ordering assertions on transport calls only, rejected because they cannot see whether an eligible permission prompt was queued at the moment an ordinary message went out. Harness killed 3/3 injected mutations (fairness before permission, no same-topic guard, capacity 7).

Inline bash heredoc feeding a python patch script failed to parse in the Bash tool (unmatched quote from raw-string content); switched to writing test snippets as files and splicing them with head/cat.
